# Google Growth — full reference

> Open-source MCP server for GA4, Google Tag Manager, Search Console and AI-search readiness.

## What it is

Google Growth is a Model Context Protocol server, a CLI and an agent skill. It reads
public pages and Google APIs, computes deterministic scores, and returns the evidence
behind every finding. Writes are disabled by default and require both an environment
flag and `confirm=true`.

## GEO — AI search readiness

The audit scores a page 0–100 across eight categories: robots.txt (18), llms.txt (18),
JSON-LD (16), meta tags (14), content (12), brand and entity (10), signals (6) and AI
discovery (6). Each check reports its own evidence, and recommendations are ordered by
recoverable points rather than opinion.

Additional tools: citability (12 content methods), crawler access matrix by tier,
llms.txt drift against the sitemap, content-risk scanning and on-page competitive
positioning.

## GTM and GA4

Twenty-two Tag Manager tools cover accounts, containers, workspaces, tags, triggers,
variables, event parameters, duplicate tags, reverse lookups, built-in variables and
container audits. Page-level installation checks verify the head loader, the noscript
fallback, dataLayer order, default consent and duplicate containers.

## Interfaces

- MCP over stdio or HTTPS (`/mcp`)
- CLI: `geo-audit`, `geo-citability`, `geo-drift`, `geo-robots`, `gtm-audit`, among others
- Agent skill packaged for Claude, Codex and Agora-style skill registries

## Limits

Readiness is measured, not citations: the server never queries ChatGPT, Claude or
Perplexity. Positioning compares public copy only, with no ranking or traffic data.
The GEO rubric is adapted from the MIT-licensed geo-optimizer-skill model.
